subjects.displayTitle: The purpose of creation: knowing, loving, and helping a world to grow
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh gives a purpose for the whole of creation in a single breath: God made us to know Him and to worship Him. From those words a wider pattern unfolds. The Hidden Treasure of the old tradition loved to be known, so love lies at the root of existence; knowledge of God depends on each soul perceiving the truth through its own eyes and heart rather than by imitation; and recognition bears fruit in character, charitable deeds and the betterment of the world, which Bahá’u’lláh names among the primary reasons the world was made. A life, in this account, is a tree, and the question is what it yields: spiritual happiness is its sap, hardship borne for God trains the spirit, and an existence of a few days’ toil followed by extinction would make creation a delirium. The Qur’an adds a guard against misunderstanding: creation is for worship, yet God seeks no sustenance from His creatures, so every benefit returns to them [1]. From here the path leads toward the love of God and His love for His own Essence, the Word by which creation came to be, and the purpose religion serves in a person and in society.
subjects.arc: Begin with charitable action and the good of all, explore love and recognition as purposes, then connect worship, spiritual growth, and a life’s social fruits.

order.why: Connects the purpose of creation with love and being known.
Open with beneficent works as one stated reason for creation.
shortened: For one of the primary reasons for the creation of the world is what was mentioned - namely, that beneficent and charitable works from assured souls should be remembered and all should attain unto them.

order.why: Read the purpose of bounty and grace as willing the good of all.
Consider human beings as bringing heavenly blessings into the world.
Hear the invitation to discover the reason for one’s existence.
shortened: The peerless friend saith that the world was created and nations emerged from the realm of nothingness into being so that perchance they might discover and know the cause and reason for their existence and creation.

order.why: Make independent perception central to recognition rather than imitation.
shortened: O Hussein in Sad, He is the Mighty! It hath been known to that honored one that the purpose of creation hath ever been and shall ever be the knowledge of God, and this knowledge dependeth upon the recognition of His servants who perceive the Truth through their own vision and heart and nature, for imitation sufficeth not, whether in acceptance or rejection.

order.why: Read the Short Obligatory Prayer’s conjunction of knowing and worshipping.
shortened: I bear witness, O my God, that Thou hast created me to know Thee and to worship Thee.

order.why: Explore love as the cause of creation through the Hidden Treasure tradition.
shortened: The cause of the creation of all contingent beings has been love, as is referred to in the well-known tradition which says: "I was a Hidden Treasure and I loved to be known, and therefore I created the creation that I might be known."

order.why: Read the same tradition as testimony to the purpose of recognition.
Consider grace, generosity, and ascent in knowledge together.
shortened: The purpose of the creation of beings and the manifestation of existence hath been the bestowal of His grace and the expression of His generosity and bounty. Through His will He brought them from nothingness into being, and through His wisdom He ordained the means of glory and exaltation, that all might ascend the ladder of knowledge to that most great station of glory and supreme nobility which is the recognition of His sacred Being.

order.why: Connect bounty and loving-kindness with good character.
shortened: The primary purpose of God - exalted be His glory - in creating creation hath been the manifestation of bounty, mercy and loving-kindness, that all might be nurtured by the hands of grace and be adorned with the ornament of goodly character.

order.why: Hear creation as the revelation of grace and munificence.
Read the parallel account of bounty, power, grace, and providence.
Examine the distinction between divine purpose and benefits that return to creatures themselves.
Read knowing and worshipping together in the Bab’s words.
Hear the direct question concerning the purpose of worship.
Consider the prayer’s sequence of worship, praise, and sanctification.
Read worship beside following what has been revealed.
shortened: Thou art He Who hath created this creation for naught else save to worship Thee, to glorify Thee, to sanctify Thee, and to follow that which hath been sent down from Thee from the places of Thy holy eternity and the wonders of Thy glorious oneness.

order.why: Hear the visitation Tablet’s account of creation in truth.
Keep the prayer’s language of recognition, detachment, and firmness in its devotional setting.
shortened: O my God! Thou didst not create anything except for those who know Thee and proclaim Thy unity and prostrate themselves before Thee and are detached from all else and stand firm in Thy Cause.

order.why: Retain the direct statement of knowledge as creation’s purpose.
Read the fashioning of Adam within the same purpose.
shortened: The purpose of the creation of the world and the fashioning of Adam hath been the knowledge of the True One, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Consider the inclusion of all servants and handmaidens.
shortened: All the world and its servants and handmaidens have been brought from nothingness into being specifically for the knowledge of God, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Hear the concise affirmation of servants created for recognition.
Read the direct address to those created for knowledge.
shortened: I created you for My recognition, would that ye might know.

order.why: Consider knowledge and the Cause together.
Hear knowledge and praise joined.
shortened: There hath been and continues to be no doubt that the purpose of creation hath been the knowledge and praise of the Beloved of the worlds.

order.why: Keep the address to Kazim in its personal setting.
Retain the brief first-person statement of creation for knowledge.
shortened: I created creation for My knowledge.

order.why: Read recognition as the stated reason for the edifice of existence.
shortened: Being hath come into existence from the realm of nothingness for the purpose of recognition. Were it not for this purpose, this mighty edifice would not have been raised up and these things would not have been witnessed.

order.why: Keep the particular address to Muhammad-Sadiq within the wider theme.
Consider the account of recognition as attainment to all good.
Read revealed verses and evidences as a path toward enduring comfort.
shortened: The purpose of the creation of beings has been the knowledge of God, exalted be His glory, so that all might comprehend, through the revealed verses and manifest evidences, that which is the cause of everlasting comfort and eternal life.

order.why: Join the purpose of knowledge with the gift of dignity.
shortened: I have created all things for My Cause and brought all beings into existence for the knowledge of My Self, that We might bring them to a station of glorious dignity.

order.why: Consider recognition and the bounty ordained for creatures.
Read creation beside the provision of guidance toward its purpose.
shortened: He created and showed the way that all might attain to that which was the purpose of creation.

order.why: Connect knowledge with following the Command.
Examine the claim that knowledge is realized through what draws a person near.
shortened: He hath created creation for His knowledge and commanded them with that which draweth them nigh unto God, the Lord of all worlds. The first is not realized except through the second, as testifieth His preserved Tablet.

order.why: Read the related connection between knowledge and nearness.
shortened: He hath created creation for His knowledge and ordained for them that which draweth them nigh unto Him.

order.why: Hear knowledge and observance together.
shortened: The purpose of man's creation hath been the knowledge of the All-Merciful and the observance of whatsoever hath been sent down from the heaven of His Will.

order.why: Consider eyes, ears, and hearts in relation to signs, verses, and love.
Add the hands that grasp the Book to the account of human faculties.
Read the gift of utterance as a means of remembrance.
shortened: This is a Tablet from Us to him who hath desired the countenance of God, the Mighty, the Powerful, the Omnipotent, that he may give thanks unto God his Lord and make mention of Him amidst His heedless servants. We have created man and taught him utterance that he might make mention of his Lord between the heavens and the earth.

order.why: Consider different responses to the summons of remembrance.
shortened: He hath created the world for the remembrance of the Ancient King - among men are those who are heedless, and those who have heard and hastened unto God, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Hear the world’s purpose expressed as remembrance of the Beloved.
shortened: The whole world was created that in this blessed Day it might attain to the remembrance of the Beloved.

order.why: Keep the personal recognition of remembrance and migration as two bounties.
shortened: Thou hast attained unto two supreme bounties that have no peer nor likeness: first, the mention of God, glorified be His majesty, which is the purpose for which all worlds were created, and second, migration in His path.

order.why: Read recognition and promotion of the Cause as fruits of existence.
shortened: The fruit of human existence hath ever been the recognition of God and the promotion of His Cause. Whoso hath attained thereunto hath attained unto all good.

order.why: Consider the Persian Bayan’s account of the Day of Manifestation as creation’s end.
Read the promise of that Day as addressed to all peoples.
shortened: All the peoples of the world have been created to know God, exalted be His glory and sovereignty, and all have been promised the Day of His Manifestation.

order.why: Consider expectation among young and old.
shortened: The primary purpose of creation hath been the recognition of God, and all people, both young and old, were awaiting the days of His Manifestation.

order.why: Hear the affirmation that all have a share in attainment.
shortened: All have been created for attainment unto the divine presence, and all have had and have their share of this most exalted station.

order.why: Read the ruby comparison as an image of the value of meeting the Lord.
shortened: When thou art assured of this, then consider the word of God, for He hath made the cause of the creation of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them to be thy meeting with thy Lord, as the glory thereof equalleth all else - just as, for example, a piece of ruby equalleth in value a thousand mithqals of gold.

order.why: Consider the personal desire to attain the Presence within a universal purpose.
Read recognition of the Manifestation and Dayspring of Revelation.
shortened: He hath created all things for the recognition of the Manifestation of His Self and the Dawning-Place of His Revelation.

order.why: Hear the prayer’s language of recognizing the Dawning-Place of signs.
shortened: Thou art He Who created the servants for the recognition of the Dawning-Place of Thy signs and the Dayspring of Thy clear tokens.

order.why: Read the personal testimony of being created for recognition.
shortened: I testify that Thou hast created me to know the Dayspring of Thy signs and the Dawning-Place of Thy Cause.

order.why: Consider recognition in relation to the Covenant.
Read creation for knowledge of the revealed Day.
Keep the claim about all divine Books in the source’s own voice.
Hear the call to friends concerning the promised Day.
shortened: Say: O friends! Man hath been created for this blessed and wondrous Day. Strive ye that ye may attain unto that wherefrom the fragrances of eternity are wafted.

order.why: Read the sending of Messengers as glad tidings of Revelation.
shortened: We have created creation for My days and sent the Messengers to give them the glad-tidings of this Revelation, through Whose mention the Books of God, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compelling, have been adorned.

order.why: Retain the brief statement of existence for recognition of this Day.
shortened: Existence has come forth from nothingness into the realm of being for the recognition of this Day. Whosoever has attained unto recognition is reckoned with God and is mentioned by the Supreme Pen in the Book of God.

order.why: Connect the promised Day with service.
Read the world’s service to the Cause beside the earlier prophetic promises.
shortened: The entire world hath been created for the service of God's Cause, and all the Prophets gave the people of the earth the glad-tidings of this wondrous Day, which in the holy divine Books is known as the Day of God.

order.why: Hear the call to hasten toward the purpose of creation.
shortened: Say: O servants, hasten that ye may attain to that for which ye were created from nothingness.

order.why: Consider seeking as a fire to kindle within the world.
Read recognition through the image of sealed wine.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Praise be to God that through divine bestowals and heavenly bounties thou hast attained recognition of the Manifestation of Mysteries and hast turned toward the Dawning-place of Revelation and the Rising-point of Inspiration, and hast partaken of the sealed wine, with a single drop of which none in existence can compare. That wine is the wine of the recognition of God, of which most people today are debarred and deprived. The whole world was created for it, yet they are seen to be veiled except for those souls who through His Name have detached themselves from all else and turned toward His horizon.

order.why: Join love and knowledge as the ultimate purpose.
shortened: Praise be to God that thou hast attained unto the love and knowledge of the Best-Beloved of the worlds - which is the ultimate purpose of creation - and hast quaffed the pure wine in the days of His manifestation.

order.why: Keep the personal acknowledgment of attainment as an expression of loving-kindness.
shortened: O my leaf, upon thee be My glory and My loving-kindness! Praise be to God, thou hast attained unto that for which existence itself came into being.

order.why: Read gratitude for assistance alongside the source’s account of deprivation.
shortened: Praise the Beloved of the world Who assisted you in a Cause from which most people are deprived and veiled, although all have been created for His recognition and His Day.

order.why: Consider perseverance despite the turning away of others.
Keep the lament concerning denial after manifestation in its own voice.
shortened: I created creation for My knowledge, yet when I manifested My Self they denied and turned away, save whom God, the King, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed, desired.

order.why: Read heedlessness through scattered rays and distant perfume.
Consider purification and the limits of worldly possession.
shortened: The purpose of man's existence hath been that, through the grace of the All-Merciful, he should be cleansed and purified from the defilements of creation, that he might become worthy to appear before the Greater Manifestation and enter the immortal celestial dominion of God. Should any soul fail to attain this station, no benefit would accrue to him even if he were to possess the whole earth and whatsoever is therein.

order.why: Read divine ordinances as directed toward elevation of souls.
shortened: The Truth, exalted be His station, whatever He hath ordained and doth ordain hath been and shall be for the elevation of souls.

order.why: Join that elevation with knowledge of what helps and harms.
shortened: The purpose of sending the Messengers and revealing the Books hath been and still is the elevation of souls and the advancement of knowledge, that all may testify to the oneness and singleness of God and become aware of that which profiteth or harmeth them.

order.why: Keep the reported equal concern for harm to oneself and to a neighbor.
shortened: This is because the purpose of Divine law is the education of all -- others as well as oneself -- and, in the sight of God, the harm done to one individual or to his neighbour is the same and is reprehensible in both cases.

order.why: Explore the expansive account of spiritual happiness and love.
shortened: As to spiritual happiness, this is the true basis of the life of man because life is created for happiness, not for sorrow; for pleasure, not for grief.

This happiness is the fundamental basis from which man is created, worlds are originated, the contingent beings have existence and the world of God appears like unto the appearance of the sun at mid-day.
This happiness is but the love of God.
This happiness is but the eternal might the brilliant traces of which are shining forth unto the temples of unity.
Were it not for this happiness the world of existence would not have been created.

order.why: Read the argument that a finite account of life cannot supply creation’s intended result.
Consider the reported fruitless-tree analogy for the need of a spiritual result.
Keep the public address’s conditional argument about physical life attributed.
shortened: If the aim were this physical life only, then this creation would be in vain and men would not have more honor or be nobler than other creatures.

order.why: Hear the concise assertion of purpose in existing things.
Consider the reported interconnection of beings and the limits of knowing a member’s uses.
Attribute the statement about inhabited luminous bodies rather than presenting it as established astronomy.
Read the reported invitation to seek wisdom and move forward.
Keep the reported harsh image of material absorption in its own historical voice.
Read the related reported contrast between outward beauty and human perfections.
Consider the reported orientation toward eternal life and spiritual virtues.
Hear the reported fruit of movement from darkness toward light.
shortened: This is the fruit of the tree of creation - to be freed from the darkness of the planet in order to enter the worlds of light. This is the object of existence; this is the fruit of the tree of humanity.

order.why: Read the reported expansion of thought and comprehension, preserving its omission.
shortened: The Baha'i Movement bestows upon man a new spirit, a new light and a new motion. It enlarges the sphere of thought. It illumines the horizon of the intellect. It expands the arena of comprehension. This is the ultimate goal of human life. This is the fruit of existence. This is the brilliant pearl of cosmic consciousness. This is the shining star of spiritual destiny...

order.why: Explore the reported water and bread images of continuing spiritual growth.
shortened: May you become thirsty for the water of Reality! May you become hungry for the Bread of the Kingdom! It was in this instance that His Holiness Christ says: He that drinketh of this water shall never thirst! This means the infinite bestowals of God; the virtues of the Divine world, the perfections of the world of humanity and the ideals of the heavenly realm.
This is the ultimate result of human life! This is the fruit of existence!

order.why: Consider new fruit as the manifestation of hidden gifts.
Read the reported relation between divine likeness and service.
shortened: But the Almighty fashioned man in his own image and likeness for the [sake] of His Love, for drawing the lights of divine virtues, for the manifestation of the celestial power, for the appearance of the efficacy of the Holy Spirit and for the projection of the ideals names and qualities of Divinity. He has ordained the subservience of all the contingent beings to man, but He hath chosen man for His own service.

order.why: Consider the reported image of earth as a workshop for character.
Read the account of growth through hardship beside the earlier affirmations of happiness and good.
shortened: If one were to ponder and reflect, which is better: to consummate one's days amidst tests and trials sustained for the love of God, or to pass them on the bed of ease? When both kinds of days have drawn to a close, the first is to be preferred, for assuredly the fruit of the tree of life is to train the spirit of man, while the second is not even worth mentioning, since it will be the cause of sorrow and regret.

order.why: Keep the reported invitation to judge by realities and fruits in its own terms.
Hear the reported practical purpose of ideas in the world’s prosperity.
Read ease, comfort, and progress as a divine purpose.
shortened: The purpose of God--glorified be His majesty--in creating the means of heaven and earth hath been the ease, comfort and progress of His servants.

order.why: Consider creation as a means of the world’s development.
Join the reformation of the world with refinement of souls.
Read world reform beside the education of peoples.
shortened: O Suhrab! God, exalted be His Glory, hath manifested Himself for the reformation of the world and the education of its peoples.

order.why: Hear the concise statement of betterment and edification.
shortened: We desire naught on earth save the betterment of the world and the edification of its peoples.

order.why: Connect recognition, exaltation of the Word, reform, and education.
shortened: All have been created for the knowledge of God, exalted be His glory, and the exaltation of His Word, and likewise have they been brought from nothingness into being for the reformation of the world and the education of its peoples.

order.why: Keep the critique of rulers and clergy attributed while reading the stated social purpose.
shortened: The kings saw no benefit for themselves in acknowledging Him, and likewise the ministers and clergy, even though in the divine Books and Scriptures the Purpose has been clearly and explicitly made manifest, and the True One has proclaimed in the most exalted utterance that this supreme Manifestation has come for the reformation of the world and the advancement of the peoples.

order.why: Consider purification from hatred as a condition of unity.
Read tranquility through harmony and counsel.
shortened: His purpose hath been the reformation of the world and the tranquility of nations. This reformation and tranquility shall not appear except through unity and harmony, and this shall not be achieved except through the counsels of the Most Exalted Pen.

order.why: Close the substantive inquiry with fellowship, freedom from tyranny, and oneness.
shortened: Today We summon all to love, unity, fellowship and concord, that perchance through the light of assured souls the horizons may be cleansed and sanctified from the darkness of tyranny, and all may acknowledge the oneness and singleness of God, exalted be His glory, and attain unto the ultimate purpose of creation.

order.why: End with the preserved brief glad tidings of what is ordained for humanity.

questions: How do charitable action, good character, and the betterment of the world enlarge the meaning of knowing and worshipping God?
What might it mean to investigate the purpose of one’s life through personal perception rather than inherited acceptance or rejection?
How does Qur’an 51:56–58 invite reflection on worship when God is understood to need nothing from His creatures?
What relationships do you find among spiritual happiness, comfort, sacrifice, and growth through difficulty?
Which fruits of a life would these readings encourage you to notice that conventional measures of success might overlook?
How could an understanding of shared purpose influence the way a community approaches education, fellowship, and the removal of harm?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 51:56–58 · Worship and divine sufficiency
references.note: Read Pickthall’s rendering of verse 56, then follow the adjacent links to verses 57 and 58. Creation for worship is followed by the declaration that God seeks no livelihood or food from creatures and is Himself the giver of livelihood. Compare this with the compilation’s account of benefits returning to human beings through recognition, gratitude, and good conduct.

subjects.displayTitle: Cultivating the soul: hidden capacities and the care that helps them grow
subjects.introduction: Anyone can till soft ground free of thorns, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observes; the skill of the divine Farmer shows in hard soil, ploughed, watered and sown until it bears. The heart, in the Bahá’í writings, is such a field. Bahá’u’lláh calls it the earth in which God has deposited the seeds of His knowledge and love, and bids His followers sow wisdom there and water it with certitude, so that hyacinths spring from the heart and not from mire. Planting, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá warns, is the easy part; strengthening roots is the long labour, and the gardener must cut away withered branches and pull the weeds of self and passion before the trees can fruit for the benefit of others. Beneath black earth lie flowers no one has yet seen, which is why a child’s purity, a seeker’s readiness and a neglected opportunity all belong to the same story. The sower of Luke’s parable, with his shallow ground, his thorns and his patient good soil, keeps the stakes of receptivity in view [1]. The way leads on to the Manifestation of God as gardener, to education and the unfolding of capacity, to the fruit by which a life is known, and back to the old question of original sin and what is truly given at birth.
subjects.arc: Begin with hope for difficult ground and the patience of cultivation, then explore preparation, sustaining care, signs of growth, and fruits of benefit to others.

order.why: Consider the hidden flowers and powers within the soil of human hearts.
Open with the divine Farmer’s capacity to cultivate difficult soil.
Read the reported winter scene as an invitation to trust growth not yet visible.
shortened: See in the winter how bare and lifeless the trees and plants seem, without leaves and without fruit. Suppose one should pass by at this time who knew nothing of the condition of the earth and saw a man ploughing it up and casting grain in the furrow. Would he not say, "How foolish this man is. He is troubling himself for no result, working for no purpose and wasting that which would give him food"? But in due time the showers descend upon the earth, the sun shines, the breezes blow and we see the result in great beauty and production.

order.why: Distinguish the ease of planting from the difficulty of sustained cultivation.
Read cultivation as increasing human bounty and blessing.
shortened: Human reality is like pure soil - the more thou dost dig and till and turn it over, the greater becomes its bounty and blessing, and the better its vegetation grows.

order.why: Keep the reported distinction between strengthening individuality and stifling its qualities.
shortened: For if he acquire praiseworthy virtues, these strengthen the individuality of man and call forth his hidden forces; but if he acquire defects, the beauty and simplicity of the individuality will be lost to him and its God-given qualities will be stifled in the foul atmosphere of self.
A fruitless tree under the influence of a wise gardener becomes fruitful; a slab of marble under the hand of a sculptor becomes a beautiful statue.

order.why: Consider the reported affirmation of a child’s original purity.
Read the reported distinction between innate capacity and what cultivation brings forth.
Consider the chapter’s argument for the need of an educator.
shortened: If the land is deprived of a cultivator, it becomes a thicket of thriving weeds, but if a farmer is found to cultivate it, the resulting harvest provides sustenance for living things. It is therefore evident that the land is in need of the farmer's cultivation.

order.why: Read the public address’s agricultural analogy within its argument about human education.
Keep the reported need to cultivate potentialities explicit.
shortened: Each kingdom of nature holds potentialities and each must be cultivated in order to reach its fulfillment.

order.why: Hear the call to seek capacity and develop readiness.
shortened: Therefore, man must seek capacity and develop readiness.
We must make the soil of our hearts receptive and fertile by tilling in order that the rain of divine mercy may refresh them and bring forth roses and hyacinths of heavenly planting.

order.why: Hear the public address’s hope for hearts carefully tilled and prepared.
Read the hope that capacity itself will grow day by day.
Consider preparation before sowing.
Read the increasing work of knowledge and wisdom in the soil of souls.
shortened: The more the farmer of knowledge and wisdom strives in the soil of souls, the more the bounties and blessings will increase. Until the earth becomes pure and ready through the efforts of the farmer, it will not yield complete fruits and great harvests will not be obtained.

order.why: Explore the Hidden Words’ seeds of wisdom and waters of certitude in all retained selections.
Read the heart as earth while noting that this is one of countless meanings.
shortened: "By the earth and its expanse" - The meaning of "earth" is the earth of hearts, which is vaster than earth and heaven, for the heart is the Most Great Throne for the establishment of thy Lord's revelation, Creator of nations and Fashioner of bones. Verily it is the earth wherein God hath deposited the seeds of His knowledge and love, that from it may spring forth the ears of knowledge and certitude. Say: O people! Today is the day of sowing. Sow ye in your hearts, with the hands of certitude, that which ye have been given by your Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. For "earth" there are countless meanings, and We have chosen but one of them.

order.why: Consider how the soil itself is changed through revelation.
shortened: Know thou, that upon whatever hearts the bountiful showers of mercy, raining from the "heaven" of divine Revelation, have fallen, the earth of those hearts hath verily been changed into the earth of divine knowledge and wisdom. What myrtles of unity hath the soil of their hearts produced!

Consider now, were the parched and barren soil of these hearts to remain unchanged, how could they ever become the recipients of the revelation of the mysteries of God, and the revealers of the divine Essence? Thus hath He said: "On the day when the earth shall be changed into another earth."

order.why: Hear rivers of utterance as nourishment for understanding.
shortened: Say: We have caused the rivers of Divine utterance to proceed out of Our throne, that the tender herbs of wisdom and understanding may spring forth from the soil of your hearts.

order.why: Read spring showers beside purification and true understanding.
Consider the relation between bounty and receptivity.
Read the removal of worthless thoughts as preparation of the heart.
shortened: No matter how much the cloud may rain, the sun may shine and the breezes blow, the soil that is sterile will give no growth.
We must endeavor to free the soil of the hearts from useless weeds and sanctify it from the thorns of worthless thoughts in order that the cloud of mercy may bestow its power upon us.

order.why: Keep the gardens explicitly identified as hearts and the weeds as self and passion.
shortened: O friends! Tend ye the gardens of the Lord of creation and keep them pure from the thorns and weeds that have grown therein. These gardens are your hearts. Whosoever hath planted the tree of divine love in the garden of his heart must needs preserve it, water it with the rain of remembrance, and keep it pure from the weeds of self and passion.

order.why: Read the warning of unfruitfulness beside the opening hope for difficult soil.
Consider the source’s contrasting soils as an occasion for gratitude and reflection.
Keep the Quranic allusion and particular address to Anarak in their own setting.
Read the reported seeds on paths, rocks, and good ground beside the Gospel comparison.
Keep the reported judgments about educational readiness attributed to their source.
Consider the reported image of all people as gardeners.
shortened: Look at the people of the world. Look in a very careful way and then you will observe that all the people are like gardeners. They are all planting the seed in a fertile ground or a very weak ground. The seed sown in sterile ground will not bear fruit--no result.

order.why: Hear the emphasis on the planter when tree, earth, and water are present.
Identify the seeds explicitly as good attributes, deeds, character, and words.
shortened: Now that the clouds of loving providence are pouring forth and the Sun of Truth is shining, now that the breezes of His Providence are blowing in this season of Divine Spring every spiritual farmer must scatter seeds of the spirit too so that he might attain onto true happiness and salvation.
Such seeds, as ordained by the one true God, are none other than goodly attributes and goodly deeds, goodly character and goodly words.

order.why: Read the pure seed of divine love.
shortened: That pure seed is the love of God which must be sown in the field of hearts so that a harvest may be reaped at the end of spring.

order.why: Consider trustworthiness as a seed worth planting.
shortened: Today good soil is rare - blessed is he who findeth it and planteth therein the seed of trustworthiness.

order.why: Keep the reported seeds of loyalty in their distinct wording.
Read faith and certitude through the image of a growing harvest.
Hear the supplication for seeds of knowledge to flourish.
Consider the work of sowing love and watering with knowledge.
Read wisdom and holy words as living waters for a sapling’s roots.
Keep the reported commission to tend seedlings until they bear fruit.
Consider service through the mysteries within the Books.
shortened: "Arise to serve the Cause of God in the vineyard of God and water the developed and flourishing trees with the waters of mysteries which are deposited in the innermost parts of the words of the Books; and be assured that the fountain of assurance will gush out in the hearts of the firm and steadfast women believers, and the divine graces will strengthen them from all sides, and the Lord will enable them to diffuse the fragrances.

order.why: Read care of tender shrubs as an ongoing responsibility.
shortened: Strive ye that they may grow very quickly. Water ye that field and take care of the tender shrubs planted by the hand of 'Abdu'l-Baha so that they may yield luscious fruits, and become the fruit of the spirit.

order.why: Hear the invitation to water the divine Farmer’s field.
Consider gardeners who train human souls and bring forth varied flowers.
Read the personal call to become a shower of bounty for others.
Explore service in the orchard and the possibility of becoming a whole garden.
shortened: Praise be unto God! who hath created sanctified souls, illumining them with the reflections of the Sun of Truth, and raising certain persons for the service of the Kingdom and gardening in the divine orchard.
This very fact denotes that, God willing, thou art to be a fruitful tree; nay, rather, thou wilt become a rose-garden of the hyacinths of realities and significances.

order.why: Connect dew upon the human heart with justice, fidelity, and humility.
shortened: Be an ornament to the countenance of truth, a crown to the brow of fidelity, a pillar of the temple of righteousness, a breath of life to the body of mankind, an ensign of the hosts of justice, a luminary above the horizon of virtue, a dew to the soil of the human heart, an ark on the ocean of knowledge, a sun in the heaven of bounty, a gem on the diadem of wisdom, a shining light in the firmament of thy generation, a fruit upon the tree of humility.

order.why: Read arts, sciences, and divine knowledge as parts of fruitful development.
shortened: It is my hope that thou wilt become a child of the Kingdom, wilt study arts, sciences and divine knowledge, mayest turn into a fruitful and flourishing tree in the Vineyard of God and that, through the sprinkling of the clouds of His loving providence, thou mayest appear in the utmost freshness and tender beauty.

order.why: Keep the reported appeal for love to awaken hearts into activity.
Consider an effort as a seed whose harvest is still to come.
Hear the account of a harvest drawing near after grace and cultivation.
Let the questions about life’s eventual fruit sharpen the inquiry.
shortened: When this cup of life overfloweth, this robust body becometh weak and incapacitated, and this vibrant morning turneth into a dark night, what fruit wilt thou pluck from the tree of life, what result wilt thou attain, what nectar wilt thou taste, from what snare wilt thou be delivered, and from what chalice wilt thou quaff?

order.why: Read forbearance, submission, and knowledge as features of a human tree.
shortened: O Muhammad-Husayn! Man is, in the sight of God, even as a tree. His leaves are forbearance and submission, and his fruits are the knowledge of the All-Bountiful Lord.

order.why: Consider deeds and spiritual qualities as leaves and branches.
shortened: Consider man as a tree: its fruit hath been and ever shall be the knowledge of God, and its leaves and branches are goodly deeds and spiritual qualities.

order.why: Read fruit explicitly as beneficial to hearts and souls.
Consider the protection of maturing fruits through remembrance.
shortened: O Majid!

With My own hands have I reared thee, and in My exalted Paradise have I planted thee, that through My loving care thou mightest bring forth goodly branches, pure boughs, and blessed fruits. And now is the time of thy fruition. Beware lest thou suffer thy leaves, fruits and branches to be withered by the scorching winds of extinction or be brought to naught. Therefore, through remembrance of My glorious Name, keep fresh the fruits of thine own tree and preserve them from violent gales and destroying tempests.

order.why: Hear remembrance and praise described as spring rain.
shortened: I swear by His peerless Beauty that mention and praise of Him, like the spring rain, makes verdant and joyous the gardens of hearts and bestows abundant blessing upon the field of realities.

order.why: Read fresh grace and spirituality as a continuing daily acquisition.
shortened: You have drunk from the Living Waters and grown and developed through the clear waters and the pure springs of certitude. Now you must ever be stirred and moved by the breezes of bounty from the direction of divine favors, and day by day acquire fresh grace, delicacy and spirituality, so that you may adorn the Abha Paradise with holy fragrances.

order.why: Consider striving and certitude through a drop’s movement toward the ocean.
Explore the seed’s relation to the whole tree and the invitation to emulate encompassing bounty.
Read humanity as trees sharing an orchard, sun, and rain.
Consider the extended springtime image of renewed minds and inward activity.
shortened: In the same way the Sun of Reality, when it illumines the horizon of the inner world, animates, vivifies and quickens with a divine and wonderful power. The trees of human minds clothe themselves in new and verdant robes, putting on leaves and blossoms and bearing spiritual fruits of the heavenly glad tidings. Then fragrant flowers of inner significances appear from the soil of human souls, and the whole being of man awakens to a new and divine activity. This is the growth and development of the inner world through the effulgent light of divine guidance and the heat of the fire of the love of God.

order.why: Read the heart’s dependence on bounty through rain and sunlight.
shortened: The spirit of man must acquire its bounties from the Kingdom of God in order that it may become the mirror and manifestation of lights and the dawning point of divine traces, because the human reality is like the soil. If no bounty of rain descends from heaven upon the soil, if no heat of the sun penetrates, it will remain black, forbidding, unproductive; but when the moistening shower and the effulgent glow of the sun's rays fall upon it, beautiful and redolent flowers grow from its bosom.

order.why: Hear the transformation of a tiny seed into a mighty tree.
shortened: For the bounty of the cloud, the effulgence and heat of the sun and the breath of the vernal zephyrs can transform the tiny seed and develop it into a mighty tree.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between dark soil and colorful flowers in its own setting.
shortened: Although the earth is the black soil, yet through the downpour of rain and the heat of the sun, flowers and anemones shall grow therefrom.

order.why: Read delicate hues emerging through shower, light, and breeze.
shortened: Although the black soil has no value or price, yet through the downpour of the vernal shower, the heat and rays of the most great, heavenly luminary and the wafting of the spring breeze the flowers and hyacinths of wonderful and delicate hues grow therein.

order.why: Consider the reported return from a visit with renewed life and wisdom.
Hear the reported identification of gardens with hearts and souls.
shortened: My gardens are the hearts and souls. The hearts are everlasting rose gardens.

order.why: Retain the image of spirits refreshed by gardens and fountains.
shortened: And spirits are stirred by the breezes of their gardens, delighting in the bounties of their realities, rejoicing in the freshness of their meadows, gladdened by the fragrance of their thickets, made happy by the outpouring from their fountains.

order.why: Read the poem’s rose, nightingale, and ascent as devotional imagery.
Explore the qualification of the saying that one flower does not make spring.
Keep the brief statement about realized qualities and the Best of Creators.
shortened: If its characteristics and conditions become fully realised in a soul then the utterance "Blessed be God, the Best of Creators" will be manifest and evident.

order.why: Read the fertile soil and polished mirror together.
shortened: Therefore, give thanks unto God that thy pure heart was a polished mirror that became illumined with the lights of guidance, and thy soul was good and fertile soil that, through the outpourings of the clouds of grace, brought forth the flowers and sweet herbs of guidance.

order.why: Hear the tender plant’s joy under guidance.
shortened: O thou tender plant in the Garden of God! Happy art thou, Happy art thou! That thou art nurtured and developed by the outpouring of the Cloud of the Most Great Guidance; art stirred into cheerfulness by the wafting of the Breeze of the Divine Spring and art adorned with foliage and blossoms by the gentle rays of the Sun of Truth.

order.why: Consider the hope for a fruit-laden tree of knowledge.
Read the sapling of love and its sweet fruit.
shortened: But you are a sapling in the garden of love. I hope that you will grow and develop through the drops of the cloud of grace and will put forth leaves and blossoms from the breeze of divine bestowal and will yield sweet and sugary fruit.

order.why: Consider freshness that adorns the realm of existence.
shortened: O spiritual friends! The souls who in this age and century have been raised up under the shade of the Word of Unity are like trees planted in the Abha Paradise. Therefore they must, through the bounty of the clouds of mercy, attain such freshness and delicacy that they adorn the realm of existence and become the envy of gardens and meadows.

order.why: Hear strong hopes addressed to a young and tender sapling.
shortened: O young and lowly servant! Although thou art but a tender sapling in the garden of the love of the Most Great Oneness, yet we cherish strong hopes that, through the great bounty and profound favor of the Lord, the Gracious One, thou wilt become a fruitful tree in the meadow and garden of the knowledge of God, and wilt become a crimson tulip, growing and flourishing and casting a far-reaching shade.

order.why: Read the acknowledgment of growth beside a stream of certitude.
Consider the summons to blossom after the gifts of cloud, sun, and wind.
Hear the prayer for a developing branch with wide reach.
Read understanding and unity as a garden in which to flourish.
shortened: Mayest thou grow and develop in the meadow of graces and become green and verdant in the orchard of understanding; in the Garden of Oneness mayest thou become the incomparable tree and the flower of the Court of Unity.

order.why: Keep the personal exchange of flowers as a sign of remembered hearts.
Turn toward the prayer for withered plants to grow again.
shortened: The plants that have sprung forth, O my Lord, in the hearts of Thy loved ones have withered away. Send down upon them, from the clouds of Thy spirit, that which will cause the tender herbs of Thy knowledge and wisdom to grow within their breasts.

order.why: Hear the request for a faithful soul and revived spirit.
shortened: Make my heart to be a pure mirror and my soul faithful. Torment Thou my insistent self, kindle my heart and revive my spirit.

order.why: Read the tiny seed’s dependence on mercy.
shortened: I am, O my God, but a tiny seed which Thou hast sown in the soil of Thy love, and caused to spring forth by the hand of Thy bounty. This seed craveth, therefore, in its inmost being, for the waters of Thy mercy and the living fountain of Thy grace. Send down upon it, from the heaven of Thy loving-kindness, that which will enable it to flourish beneath Thy shadow and within the borders of Thy court.

order.why: Consider the grove’s plea not to be abandoned.
shortened: We are saplings which have been planted by the fingers of Thy bounty and have been formed out of the water and clay of Thy tender affection. We thirst for the living waters of Thy favours and are dependent upon the outpourings of the clouds of Thy generosity. Abandon not to itself this grove wherein our hopes aspire, nor withhold therefrom the showers of Thy loving-kindness.

order.why: Hear the prayer for growth and abundant harvests.
Read the wish to be refreshed by the garden of another heart.
Consider the sweet basil and branch beside pools of mercy.
Hear the prayer for saplings to develop and bear fruit.
shortened: O Lord! Through the outpouring of the cloud of Thy bounty, the heat of the Sun of Reality, and the wafting of the breeze of guidance, grant these saplings growth and development. Bestow upon them freshness and grace, that they may bring forth leaves and blossoms and yield fruit.

order.why: Read the hope for hearts to become a flourishing garden.
shortened: I beseech God that through the bounty of the Most Great One and the grace and mercy of the Supreme Concourse, the garden of hearts may be so adorned as to become the envy of the most verdant garden and the object of jealousy of the Paradise of Abha.

order.why: Consider the seed planted in the soil of unity.
Hear the prayer for knowledge, love, and praise to grow.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Thou through Whose word the world was set in motion and by Whose name the Ancient Sea was made to surge, to send down from the heaven of Thy grace and the clouds of Thy mercy that which will cause to spring forth from the soil of hearts the plants of Thy knowledge and the fruits of Thy love and praise.

order.why: Uses ploughing and fertilizing the soil as an image of the love of God working in hearts.
Read the request that a plant not be deprived of rain.
shortened: Thou knowest, O my God, that this is a plant which hath grown in the soil of Thy acceptance - withhold not from it the rain from the clouds of Thy grace and the heaven of Thy generosity.

order.why: Close the linked devotional sequence with a plea for unity’s fruits for servants and kindred.
shortened: Behold, then, O my God, my loneliness among Thy servants and my remoteness from Thy friends and Thy chosen ones. I beseech Thee, by the showers of the clouds of Thy mercy, whereby Thou hast caused the blossoms of Thy praise and utterance and the flowers of Thy wisdom and testimony to spring forth in the hearts of all them that have recognized Thy oneness, to supply Thy servants and my kindred with the fruits of the tree of Thy unity, in these days when Thou hast been established upon the throne of Thy mercy.

order.why: Retain the source passage’s incomplete opening while reading the tree reaching toward heaven.
Read the supplied reported image of pruning and abundant fruit.
Consider the supplied account of human fruits and sacred words, keeping its wording and omission.
Read the supplied guidance on care, protection, and education of children.
End with the supplied practical cultivation through prayer, meditation, study, and service.

questions: What does the opening image of skillful work with difficult soil suggest about people whose capacities are not yet apparent?
How do divine bounty, personal effort, education, and patient companionship contribute different parts of growth?
Which seeds, weeds, roots, and fruits in these readings have recognizable counterparts in everyday life?
How does Luke 8:4–15 deepen the distinction between receiving a word with initial enthusiasm and bearing fruit with patience?
What care might be needed after a promising beginning, especially when growth seems slow or has withered?
How can the fruits of inward cultivation become beneficial to other people while respecting their individuality?

references.label: 1 · Luke 8:4–15 · The sower and patient fruitfulness
references.note: Read the King James Version’s parable and its explanation. Notice the seed identified with the word of God, the hazards of shallow roots and crowding thorns, and the patient fruitfulness of a good heart. Compare these images with the compilation’s emphasis on preparation, continued tending, and the possibility of cultivating difficult soil.

subjects.displayTitle: Belief and denial: hearing a call and learning to recognize it
subjects.introduction: Some heard the Call and turned toward it, Bahá’u’lláh writes; some heard and turned away; and some never heard at all. That threefold sorting puts the weight of the matter on what happens after hearing, and it unsettles every assumption about who will recognize a new revelation. God’s remembrance of His servants precedes their remembrance of Him, yet not every ear catches it: the learned were held back while a handmaiden answered, the mature were deprived while a suckling child drank the milk of recognition, and divines who had pleaded for thirteen hundred years that God hasten the Promised One rejected Him when the light dawned. Rank, learning, prior devotion and outward possession all fail as guarantees; what counts is turning, and then remaining steadfast when imaginings, desires and the opinions of others pull the other way. The Gospel of John tells of a world that did not know the Word and of those who received Him being born of God, a kindred account of familiarity failing and strangers believing [1]. The sources’ stark contrasts of paradise and fire belong to their own urgent voice, and they ask to be read as a mirror. The path continues into the life of the spirit, the imagery of light and darkness, and the measure of nearness and remoteness.
subjects.arc: Begin by distinguishing hearing from response, explore the limits of rank and inherited expectation, then read the sources’ contrasts of life and denial alongside steadfastness, action, and prayer.

order.why: Open with the explicit distinction among response, rejection, and not having heard.
shortened: Among the people are those who have heard the Call and turned towards it, and among them are those who heard and turned away, and among them are those who did not hear. Thus has the matter been detailed in a Clear Tablet.
Those who denied the Proof of God and His evidence, and turned towards every distant idolater, have indeed suffered loss.

order.why: Read chosen faith beside existential faith and natural obedience.
Consider divine remembrance preceding human hearing and perception.
Read the contrast between learned status and a handmaiden’s response.
shortened: How many a learned one was prevented, and how many a handmaiden heard and responded and turned unto the Dawning-Place of the manifestation of her Lord, the All-Forgiving, the All-Bountiful!

order.why: Consider mature people and infants as images of unexpected recognition.
Examine the claim that prior religious diligence does not guarantee acceptance.
Read the invitation to come, hear, and see beside the Kitab-i-Badi’s claims of certitude.
shortened: Know this much: that in the station of certitude, doubt has no place. If you say that recognition of this new Revelation has become confused for this servant, then come forth to witness. If you say there is confusion in the revealed verses, then come forth to hear and see. If you say confusion exists in deeds, know that every doer's deeds depend on His command and are contingent on His permission. The station of absolute certainty is sanctified above the doubts and imaginings of the worlds and those who are deluded.

order.why: Consider recognition as the source’s criterion for true religious learning.
shortened: Whosoever among the divines of every age receiveth, in the Day of Reckoning, the testimony of faith from the Source of true knowledge, he verily becometh the recipient of learning, of divine favor, and of the light of true understanding. Otherwise, he is branded as guilty of folly, denial, blasphemy, and oppression.

order.why: Read the contrast between response and pride in authority.
shortened: How many a servant hath heard the call and responded to his Ancient Lord, and how many a one robed in authority hath disdained and waxed proud before God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Keep the account of prolonged expectation followed by rejection in its polemical setting.
Read the call to peace and human oneness beside the chapter’s account of rejection.
shortened: Now Baha'u'llah has appeared, the divine teachings and admonitions have been unveiled, the call of the oneness of humanity has been sounded, the banner of the kingdom of peace is flying, and the tabernacle of love and harmony amongst all mankind has been raised in the very heart of the world and is summoning all people. And yet again some ignorant souls imagine that these divine teachings are without foundation and regard their own imaginations as lofty thoughts. But before long it will become manifest that what He has proclaimed is sound, proven, and compelling, and that all other thoughts are vain and idle.

order.why: Consider the opposing responses to the Apostle and Seal of the Prophets.
shortened: One raised the cry of "but He is the Apostle of God and the Seal of the Prophets," while another loudly proclaimed "he hath fabricated against God."

order.why: Retain the dismissive phrase about ancient tales as a reported response.
shortened: Among the people are those who heard the call and responded, turning their faces toward Him Who created earth and heaven, saying "Our Lord, we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying 'Believe in your Lord,' so we believed." And among them are those who persisted and said "This is nothing but tales of the ancients."

order.why: Hear the invitation to reflect on contrasting responses in every age.
shortened: Should one reflect upon the appearance of the Suns of Truth, it becomes clear and evident that in every age there have been and will be the truthful and the false. Take heed, O ye who possess insight!

order.why: Consider the need for a renewed response in each revelation.
Read the possible reversal of affirmation and negation between dispensations.
Examine the warning that a former station does not secure a present one.
Consider the reversal of worldly exaltation and abjection through recognition.
Read the repeated distinction between material possession and spiritual response.
shortened: Thou didst make Thyself known on the Day of Resurrection, whereupon those who recognized among Thy creation attained recognition, and thereby entered Thy paradise, whether they possessed all things or possessed nothing; and those who were veiled among Thy creation remained veiled and entered Thy fire, whether they possessed anything or possessed nothing.

For whoso turneth unto Thee -- even wert Thou to invest him with dominion over all that is on the earth -- Thou wouldst assuredly ordain for him guidance and faith; and if not, then nothing of it shall be his. Likewise, whosoever is veiled from Thee, Thou hast judged him to be without truth and faith, whether Thou hast granted him all things or nothing thereof.

order.why: Consider the source’s claim that response to the new revelation bears on earlier faith.
shortened: Say: If you believe in Me and My verses, then you shall attain all good, and if you believe not in Me, you have not believed in any of the Messengers, nor are you God-fearing on that Day. And you did not follow the Messengers before, nor were you certain of God.

order.why: Read present response in relation to the source’s understanding of religious continuity.
Keep the urgent judgment about hesitation within the Tablet’s theological voice.
shortened: Any soul who today, after hearing this Most Great Cause, hesitates less than a moment is not worthy of mention.

Say: The Will of God is other than your wills, and His way is other than your ways. He walks not in your paths nor follows your desires. He calls those on earth and guides them to His straight path. Whoso turns toward Him has attained all good, and whoso turns away is among the people of the fire in a mighty Book.

order.why: Read the parallel insistence on immediate response without adopting its condemnations as editorial labels.
shortened: Say: God! Then leave the ungodly in the lowest depths of hell. Say: Whoso hesitateth in this Cause, he is of the ungodly in the tablets of mighty glory. And whoso believeth in this Revelation, he is of the believers before God, thy Lord and the Lord of all creatures.

order.why: Consider the distinction drawn among recognition, turning away, and hesitation.
Examine the several obstacles named: imaginings, names, desires, and dependence on others.
shortened: Among the people are those who cling to vain imaginings, turning away from the Self-Subsisting; and among them are those who are veiled by a name from among names, disbelieving in God, the Creator of heaven; and among them are those who hold fast to their desires, heedless of guidance; and among them are those who were attracted by the breezes of revelation in such wise that they turned with steadfast mountains and took the choice wine of life in the name of the All-Merciful, detached from all else, and drank and said: "This, verily, is what was intended in the Books of God, the Most High, the Most Great."

order.why: Read contentment with one’s own imaginings beside response to the Call.
shortened: Among the people are those who heard the Call from the Supreme Horizon and turned unto Him, detached from all who are in the heavens and on earth; and among them are those who were content with their own vain imaginings and turned away from the One, the All-Informed.

order.why: Consider the influence of following an envious opponent.
shortened: How many a soul, upon hearing the Call, hath turned to the Most Exalted Horizon, and how many a soul hath turned away and followed every envious opponent.

order.why: Read the contrast between wholehearted response and following others in rejection.
Keep the account of turning back after hearing within its own setting.
shortened: Among the people are those who have heard and turned towards it, and among them are those who have turned upon their heels - these are truly among the perishing ones. They cast guidance behind their backs and took up vain desire - thus doth testify the Most Exalted Pen in this wondrous Tablet.

order.why: Consider instability and desire in the source’s criticism of changing allegiance.
shortened: Now observe how inconstant, faithless and unstable some souls are. Shame upon those who believed then disbelieved, drew near then withdrew. These are servants who incline with every wind and are moved by every fancy, supposing themselves to be guided. Nay, by the Lord of the Throne and earth! They worship their desires but know it not. Strange that after beholding the ocean of meanings and its waves, and witnessing the Sun of utterance and its effulgence, one should be deprived thereof and cling to vain desire which is utter nothingness.

order.why: Retain the particular address concerning Ahmad and its unresolved quoted ending.
shortened: Would that you had written to Ahmad himself: "We know not upon which path thou standest, nor which way thou walkest. At times we find thee repentant, penitent and remorseful, and at other times we see thee an unbeliever, a rejecter, a hypocrite and doubter.

order.why: Read the Qayyumu’l-Asma’s distinction between inner conviction and outward denial.
shortened: Among the people are those who say "We believe in God and His Most Great Remembrance," and God is ever cognizant of His servants in truth. They have disbelieved with their tongues after their souls were convinced, and God hath taught them within their own souls that they are fresh disbelievers in God, the Exalted.

O people! If ye believe in Our Remembrance after the Truth hath come unto you with the Book, ye shall be recorded in the Book of the Exalted Ones round about the Gate. And if ye deny God after He hath sent down unto you the Remembrance and this Most Great Book, ye shall be inscribed as followers of the tree of Satan in the Book of the Prison, having shown arrogance against God, the Truth.

order.why: Consider signs and ordinances beside the following of passions.
shortened: Those who believe in the signs of God and follow the ordinance of the Book -- these are the rightly guided. But those who deny the signs of thy Lord and follow their passions -- these are in manifest error.

order.why: Read response expressed through action according to the Book.
Hear the statement that commands are directed toward people’s benefit.
shortened: We have commanded all to that which profiteth them. Some have turned towards it and some have turned away, and he who turneth away is among the distracted ones.

order.why: Consider the stated effects of turmoil on seekers’ attention and capacity to hear.
shortened: But the tumult and sedition in Iran allows not the friends to draw a breath, nor leaves the seekers with attention or capacity to hear. "Sedition was dormant; God's curse be upon him who awakened it."

order.why: Read the traveller’s reversals and trials in the Four Valleys.
shortened: 16 On this plane, the traveller meeteth with many a trial and reverse. Now is he lifted up to heaven, now is he cast into the depths. As it hath been said: "Now Thou drawest me to the throne of the realms above, again Thou scorchest me in the fire of hell."

order.why: Consider tribulation as the source’s test of steadfastness.
shortened: The chalice of tribulation hath ever been reserved for the faithful, and through trials and afflictions are the steadfast distinguished from the doubters.

order.why: Keep the demanding account of cooperation, patience, and sacrifice in its own voice.
shortened: Rest and comfort and laziness and luxury and negligence and indolence can come from any soul. Indeed, in this arena everyone can show the utmost strength and power. But cooperation and mutual assistance and patience and steadfastness and sacrifice of life is not the work of every soul. This is special to blessed souls, not every ignorant fool and helpless idler.

order.why: Retain the reported fatalist’s refusal to join a fight as a distinct historical episode.
shortened: Ahmad Khan was a fatalist and did not endorse the idea 'These are the armies of God' he said 'I shall never become a party in a league to fight with them. Whenever they reach my village they are welcomed.'

order.why: Read belief as a beginning and steadfastness in love as an end, preserving the polemical closing sentence.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! The beginning of the Cause is belief in God, and its end is steadfastness in His love. The barkers are spread abroad like satans.

order.why: Consider turning, knowing, and remaining steadfast together.
shortened: The Most Exalted Pen declareth: The matter of the world to come hath been, and shall ever be, to turn unto God---glorified be His majesty---to know Him, and to remain steadfast in His Cause. Whoso attaineth unto that which hath been mentioned is, in the Clear Book, numbered and recorded among the people of certitude. Bewilderment, doubt, and the like have no place in this station.

order.why: Hear the invitation to relinquish imaginings and hold to certitude.
Read the call to receive what is offered through encompassing grace.
shortened: Cast aside doubts and idle fancies, and take hold of that which the Lord of all beings hath, out of His all-encompassing grace, sent down for you.

order.why: Consider the dust of imaginings and the light of assurance.
shortened: Those who have hesitated are they whom the dust of vain imaginings hath overtaken, whereby they were prevented from the Dayspring of inspiration.
This is the Day wherein the eye of doubt hath been blinded and the vision of certitude hath been gladdened by this Sun which hath shone forth from the horizon of assurance.

order.why: Read the contrast between wandering and attaining light.
shortened: Those who doubted are wandering in the wilderness of heedlessness. Those who turned to Him have attained the lights of certitude.

order.why: Keep the distinction between assurance and doubt in its theological setting.
Consider drinking from the ocean as an image of assured response.
Read the choice wine of certitude and participation in the utterance.
shortened: Whoso hath quaffed the choice wine of certitude, he is of the people of this utterance, and he who hath been debarred therefrom hath no portion in this perspicuous Book.

order.why: Retain the blessing and warning in the source’s own terms.
Consider deprivation through the imagery of love, grace, and mercy.
shortened: And whoso denieth Him hath been deprived of the Salsabil of My love and the Kawthar of My grace and the choice wine of My mercy - that wine by which the sincere ones were attracted and the believers soared unto the atmosphere of My loving-kindness, which none hath known save him whom We have taught through that which was revealed in My Hidden Tablet.

order.why: Read the contrasting drinks as theological images of response.
Notice the wine of life offered to all before different responses are described.
Read encompassing grace beside the distinction between turning toward and away.
shortened: This is a day wherein grace hath encompassed all religions, and the Divine Lott Tree hath called out from the Most Exalted Horizon: 'Verily, there is none other God but Him, the One, the Single, the All-Knowing.' Whoso hath turned and beheld, he hath attained unto this grace, and whoso hath turned away, he is accounted among the ungodly in My perspicuous Book."

order.why: Consider the remembrance of those who cast off imaginings.
Read a personal remembrance intended to attract and assist others.
shortened: Therefore hath the Pen of Revelation traced thy name, that its influence may attract thee in such wise as to detach thee from all who are on earth, and that through thee may be detached such servants as wander in the wilderness of error and are debarred from that which their Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, hath desired for them.

order.why: Keep the remembrance addressed to believers within its context of opposition.
shortened: We have set forth therein a matter which none hath discovered, and We have turned therein the verses as a remembrance from Our presence unto those who have believed in God and His signs, and have detached themselves from those who have disbelieved and associated partners with God and who stood at the station of opposition.

order.why: Consider remembered love and protection from whispering.
Hear the prayerful account of a servant’s path of certitude.
shortened: This is Thy servant who hath believed in Thee and loved Thy loved ones and turned away from Thine enemies and walked in the path of certitude until he reached the pivot of journeys and recognized the Manifestation of Thy Chosen Cause.

order.why: Retain the personal blessing for faith in the wondrous Day.
Read the benediction within its context of detachment from rejection.
Keep both servants and handmaidens within the account of differing responses.
Read nearness and loss as the source’s two outcomes.
Hear the concise relation of turning and drawing near.
Retain the distinction between rejecting proof and turning to the Desired One.
Affirms truth’s independence from the belief or denial of created things.
Read the contrast of rejection and the straight path.
shortened: Among the people are those who have turned away and denied God's Revelation and His proof, and among them are those who have turned towards His straight path.

order.why: Keep the brief acknowledgment that servants have responded differently.
shortened: We make mention of the servants for the sake of God - among them are those who turned away and those who turned towards Him.

order.why: Consider response to revelation in relation to truthfulness.
shortened: Among the people are those who have rejected the signs of God and His appearance, and among them are those who have hastened unto the Dawning-Place of Revelation with spirit and sweet fragrance. Blessed is the soul that hath spoken the truth, and woe unto him who hath disbelieved in God when He came with His grandeur and sovereignty.

order.why: Read differing reactions to the same rustling call.
shortened: When its rustling was lifted up, among the people some were drawn to it and hastened until they clung fast to it, while others heard and turned away until they disbelieved in God, the Lord of all worlds.

order.why: Hear the source’s contrast between nearness and idolatry.
Consider holding to the Book as a mark of belonging.
shortened: He who hath taken hold of God's Book with the hand of might is of the people of Baha, and he who hath turned away is among those who have gone astray.

order.why: Read nearness and opposition through the Tablet’s record imagery.
Keep the claim about promise and loss in its own voice.
shortened: Whoso turns to it has attained what was promised in the Book, and whoso turns away has lost in this world and the next. To this testifies the Lord of Names in this station.

order.why: Read the ranking of belief and denial as a theological judgment.
Retain the blessing and condemnation without making them editorial descriptions of people.
shortened: Blessed is he who hath turned toward Him; woe unto him who hath denied Him and turned away from that which hath been sent down from His presence. Verily he is among the most wretched of creatures.

order.why: Consider the source’s affirmation of preference for believers.
shortened: We have made manifest the Cause and made clear that which was hidden from the servants, and We have favored those who have believed over those who have denied God when He came with manifest sovereignty.

order.why: Read paradise as the stated result of turning toward the Countenance.
Hear the relation between hearing, response, and paradise or fire.
shortened: Whosoever turned towards it and attained unto hearing it, such a soul is recorded with God among the companions of the most exalted Paradise and is inscribed by the Supreme Pen. And whosoever turned away, such a soul is recorded with the Chosen One as being among the people of the Fire.

order.why: Read the prayer’s explicit binary of affirmation and negation.
Consider divine preservation and abandonment in the prayer’s theological framing.
Explore the transformed world and the imagery of higher and lower stations.
Read distinction through a word differentiated from the Mother of Verses.
Keep the account of disagreement and hatred as the source’s description of division.
shortened: The peoples shall differ regarding this Ancient Light, and hatred shall appear among them concerning this Mighty Pillar, that the good may be distinguished from the evil, and light from darkness.

order.why: Consider the two calls and the response Here am I.
shortened: Today two calls are raised: the first is the call of the All-Merciful, and the second is the call of Satan. Those souls who, upon hearing the second call, utter the word "yea" - such souls are deprived of the Kingdom of utterance and the heaven of bounty. They are the manifestations of tyranny and lewdness, and the dawning-places of infidelity and transgression. Blessed are those souls who have attained to the hearing of the first call and have responded with "Here am I, O my God, here am I!"

order.why: Read hearing joined either to faith or disobedience through scriptural allusions.
Consider hearing and spiritual life in the concise formulation.
shortened: He who hath an ear hath heard the call of God, and he who hath not heard is counted among the dead.

order.why: Read the grave imagery as a spiritual judgment on turning away.
shortened: How many a servant hath believed, and how many a servant hath turned away - and he who hath turned away is assuredly among the denizens of the graves.

order.why: Keep the distinction between God’s path and idle fancy in the source’s voice.
Consider sweetness of utterance beside the imagery of spiritual death.
shortened: Were anyone to find the sweetness of the utterance which hath proceeded from the mouth of the All-Merciful, he would abandon the world and all that is therein, turning unto God, the Mighty, the Praised. Think not that they who turned away are alive - nay, they are among the dead. Soon shall they know what hath escaped them, but today they are in a mighty veil.

order.why: Read living waters as an image of belonging and renewal.
Retain the parallel opposition of turning and spiritual death.
Read illuminated and darkened faces as figurative religious contrasts.
Keep the related face and dawn imagery in its distinct wording.
shortened: The faces of those near unto God have been illumined by the lights of the Countenance, while the faces of those who turned away have been darkened by their rejection of this Brilliant Dawn.

order.why: Consider the source’s visual imagery and its harsh comparison with bats.
shortened: Every eye and insight that possessed the power of vision was illumined, while those weak of sight and limited in insight, lacking the power of vision, shut their eyes and, like bats, crept into the cave of darkness.

order.why: Read the closed-eye image as the source’s account of failed perception.
Keep the exhortation concerning those who deny the sun in its polemical setting.
Read sight, deprivation, and exclusion as the source’s theological contrasts.
Consider the claim that rejecting the sun impairs discernment of light and darkness.
shortened: Can those who have turned away from the Countenance distinguish between light and darkness? No, by the Lord of creation! They deny the Sun and its sovereignty, the proof and its evidence, and they say that which neither the people of the Furqan nor those who turned away from God in past ages and centuries have said.

order.why: Keep the worm and owl imagery attributed rather than using it as an editorial judgment.
shortened: How can the lowly worm, whose fortified palace is the depth of earth, know aught of the musk-laden morning breeze? And what effect hath the rose garden of mystical knowledge upon the owl of the ruins of this earthly realm?

order.why: Read the contrast of nightingale and raven as polemical metaphor.
Preserve the forceful bird and beetle comparisons within their source setting.
Consider the source’s association of faith with love and denial with dissension.
shortened: For these are believers, those are deniers; these are luminous, those are in darkness; these are the dawning-places of true love, those are the manifestations of pure dissension.

order.why: Read the different inward effects attributed to the same outpouring.
shortened: The hearts of the faithful have been dilated by this all-embracing mercy from the Creator of earth and heaven, while the hearts of the unfaithful have been constricted by this all-encompassing outpouring from the Supreme Kingdom.

order.why: Hear joy and despair in the brief paired image.
Keep the account of sacrifice, union, and deprivation in its devotional intensity.
shortened: The conscious lovers and vigilant seekers were moved to ecstasy and joy, and in rapture, attraction and gladness, dancing and clapping, they hastened to the altar of love. They sacrificed soul, head and heart, offered their spirits to the Beloved, attained true union, established themselves in the court of Beauty, and were blessed with mighty triumph and abiding delight, achieving high distinction. But the false ones and pretenders remained deprived and at loss, living in regret and weeping over their state. Blind were they raised, deaf were they gathered, until that Sun of Reality was concealed behind the clouds of glory and vanished in the invisible Kingdom.

order.why: Read the blessing of faith beside the warning against vain imaginings.
Turn toward the prayerful movement from superstition and darkness into light.
shortened: This thy servant hath abandoned superstitions, emerged from darkness and hath entered into Thy Light which hath shone forth to the world!

order.why: Hear the plea to be cleansed of obstructing doubts.
shortened: I beseech Thee by this Revelation whereby darkness hath been turned into light, through which the Frequented Fane hath been built, and the Written Tablet revealed, and the Outspread Roll uncovered, to send down upon me and upon them who are in my company that which will enable us to soar into the heavens of Thy transcendent glory, and will wash us from the stain of such doubts as have hindered the suspicious from entering into the tabernacle of Thy unity.

order.why: Close with the prayer for others to receive awareness and reunion, while preserving the source’s incomplete quotation.
shortened: Today the accepting and the rejecting appear in two forms. The accepting one saith: "My God, my God! Grant Thy servants a portion from the ocean of awareness, and deprive them not of the effulgent lights of the Luminary of vision. Thou didst desire reunion; the Wronged One too desireth it, but the smoke of heedless hearts hath become an obstacle, and the hatred of souls hath appeared as an impenetrable barrier.

questions: How does the distinction between not hearing, hearing and responding, and hearing and turning away affect your reading of this subject?
Why might rank, learning, or previous devotion fail to ensure recognition of something new?
What do the images of hearing, sight, thirst, and life reveal about faith beyond verbal assent?
How does John 1:10–13 illuminate the tension between religious familiarity and receiving an unexpected revelation?
How can the sources’ urgent judgments become an occasion for examining one’s own assumptions and conduct?
What relationship do you see among chosen faith, steadfast love, cooperation, and the closing prayer for others to receive awareness?

references.label: 1 · John 1:10–13 · Recognition and receiving
references.note: Read the King James Version’s account of the world not knowing the Word and of those who receive Him becoming children of God. Notice the distinction between belonging by descent and a life born of God. Compare this with the compilation’s challenges to inherited status and prior religious confidence, while preserving the Gospel’s particular account of Christ.
